newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Rating agency says Malaysia overbuilding continues.
newsitem.headline: Rating agency says Malaysia overbuilding continues.

text.p: Rating Agency Malaysia (RAM) said on Friday that overbuilding continues in certain segments of Malaysia's construction industry.
In its quarterly report on the industry, the private rating concern said it also expects Malaysian hotel margins to be under pressure this year from oversupply.
It said that country's construction sector was expected to grow at 10.2 percent this year against 13 percent forecast by the central bank, Bank Negara Malaysia.
The construction sector grew by 13 percent in 1996.
"The construction sector recorded continuing high growth in 1996, giving rise to signs of oversupply in certain sub-sectors of the property market," the RAM report said.

But, "despite selective credit control measures introduced last year, overbuilding in certain segments of the construction sector continues, thus warranting stricter, pre-emptive actions by Bank Negara," it said.
Hotel industry will be particularly affected due to heavy new constructions taking place, particularly in and around Kuala Lumpur, for the 1998 Commonwealth Games.
"Oversupply, particularly in four and five-star hotels, will increasingly see their margins pressurised," a spokesman for RAM said.
He said there was always a situation of low occupancy and low room rates in hotels once a major international event in any city around the world.
